identity.title: LER 2021-004-01 for Susquehanna Unit 1, Loss of 1B RHRSW Pump due to Cable Damage During Excavation Activities

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of the event was determined to be that Cable FF1S0601A was struck through an inadvertent puncture of unidentified conduit F1F104 during excavation activities. The apparent cause of the failure was that methods for reviewing the condition of Cable FF1S0601A following damage were flawed, resulting in an inaccurate assessment and non-conservative decisions.
cause.theme: flawed post-damage assessment procedure led to non-conservative decision to keep cable in service

nodes.description: Personnel at SSES punctured a 4-inch conduit line during excavation activities to support unrelated piping replacement work.

nodes.display_name: Cable FF1S0601A damaged / grounded on B-phase
nodes.description: Cable FF1S0601A within conduit F1F104 was damaged by the puncture, resulting in a ground on the B-phase of the cable.

nodes.display_name: Flawed post-damage assessment led to cable remaining in service
nodes.description: Methods for reviewing the condition of Cable FF1S0601A following the September 23 damage were flawed, resulting in an inaccurate assessment and non-conservative decision not to remove the cable/pump from service.

properties.note: Unit 1 'A' RHRSW subsystem declared inoperable Sept 29 due to UHS spray array/bypass valve alignment for nozzle cleaning, concurrent with 'B' subsystem inoperability

nodes.display_name: Repair damaged conduit and replace damaged cable
Update controlled plant drawings to reflect actual field measurements
Revise station procedures to require reassessment of risk for changing field conditions and describe limitations of damage assessment methods
Technical Specification 3.7.1, RHRSW System and UHS
ADAMS Accession No. ML081000255 (accident analysis basis for 3-hour valve realignment)

chain: excavation activity punctures unidentified conduit F1F104 [cause D: flawed damage-assessment procedure] -> Cable FF1S0601A damaged/grounded on B-phase -> non-conservative decision keeps cable/pump in service -> 1B RHRSW Pump inoperable (Sept 23 - Oct 11) -> concurrent with Unit 1 'A' RHRSW subsystem inoperable (Sept 29 onward) for valve alignment [not counted as SSFF; 'A' subsystem could still perform safety function within 3-hr realignment window]
notes: The direct/apparent cause distinction in the narrative maps to a single official cause code D (Defective Procedure), governing category per the flawed damage-assessment methodology. The 'A' RHRSW subsystem inoperability was due to valve alignment for planned nozzle-cleaning maintenance, not a failure, but is modeled as a System node and Consequence because the narrative explicitly discusses its concurrent inoperability and safety significance; no BACKED_UP_BY edge asserted since 'A' subsystem was itself inoperable (valve-misaligned) during the overlap, not an operable backup. No previous occurrences reported by licensee, so no stub LER/SIMILAR_TO edge emitted.
